messages:
kavi: heads-up — after the kernel flip for opt-12-sparse we observed ~12% p99 increase on decode-heavy tails (long prompts + streaming). noticed it after the midnight canary.

elinor: ugh. which kernel path did we move to? nvfuser or the custom attention kernels? any perf counters?

kavi: nvfuser -> custom_attention hybrid. perf snapshot attached (reduced):
```
# perf counters
L2_misses: 1.2M -> 3.8M
kv_prefetch_miss: 120 -> 380
decode_cycles: +9% on tail buckets
batch_fill_rate: -3% overall
```

sam: looks like KV prefetch thrash to me — when batches coalesce long-decode tokens, the KV headroom gets exhausted and we get eviction churn. did the batcher change token_budget_target?

kavi: we did flip token_budget_target from 2800 -> 3200 globally to try and reduce microbatch churn. thinking that combined with the kernel change caused increased decode working set.

mira: suggestion: revert global bump and try per-bucket token targets instead. e.g. short/mid/long length buckets with decode-rate-aware token budgets. keeps short fast, lets long be heavier.

kavi: proposed quick config to A/B (canary):
```yaml
batch_policy: continuous
admission:
  prefer_same_decode_rate: true
buckets:
  length_buckets: [0-64,65-512,513+]
  decode_rate_buckets: [0-8,8-16,16+]
token_budget_targets:
  short: 1024
  mid: 3072
  long: 6144
kv_prefetch_headroom:
  default: 0.2
  long_decode: 0.35
```

sam: +1. Also try making kernel routing aware of batch composition: if batch has >50% long-decode, force the fallback kernel that favors larger working sets. That avoids thrash without hurting short requests.

ops-bot: deploy plan queued: canary 5% traffic -> us-west1 only. canary config: per-bucket token budgets + kv headroom bump for long decode. rollback trigger: p99 > baseline * 1.03 for 10m.

kavi: I'll run a synthetic microbench with ~10k long-tail prompts and collect per-kernel counters + batch composition histogram. uploading results to the perf drive when done.

elinor: action items: 1) microbench + kernel counters (kavi), 2) canary deploy with per-bucket token budgets (ops-bot), 3) try kernel-routing rule on coalesced long batches (sam), 4) monitor kv_prefetch_miss and batch_fill_rate (mira). rollback if p99 regress >3%.

sam: ack :thumbsup:

mira: thanks — if this looks good we should also add a regression test in the decode-rate simulator to prevent global token_budget flips without per-bucket analysis.
